text: The fight pauses at a Choose. The handler holds the rest of the fight as k.
To answer, it runs battle itself: the same function a person plays. It needs no model of the game.
For each card it can play, and for ending the turn, it plays that card on the state, then runs the rest of the fight three times.
Each run has a stack of its own, so it does not use up the dice of the paused fight.
The handler counts the wins. Here every move wins all three. The paused fight has not moved.
With a tie it keeps the first move, Bash. It resumes k with it, and the fight goes on.
On seed 3, the bot answers eleven Chooses with a hundred and sixty-five playouts, in about a fifth of a second.
